title: order-provenance-audit: artefacts, reference implementation and verification pipeline for “Silent order corruption in per-sample evaluation artefacts”
description:
Complete replication package for the manuscript Silent order corruption in per-sample evaluation artefacts: why the standard negative control cannot detect it, and two tests that can (submitted to the Journal of Systems and Software).

Contents: the per-run table for 356 single-GPU training runs across seven public forecasting benchmarks, three backbones and four plug-in arms; the 712 per-sample error vectors and the per-window feature tables they are joined against; the autocorrelation order test (AOT) with exact Wald–Wolfowitz randomisation moments and its empirical deep-tail calibration; the cross-arm agreement test (CAT); the order-provenance sidecar contract; the T1 and T2 downstream analyses with equivalence tests in three readings (paired over cells, clustered by dataset, and replicated over independent draws of the defect and of the control); the derived-label distribution table; the paired repair-cost table; a test suite that states the propositions of the paper as executable assertions; and the generators for every macro, table and figure in the manuscript.

tools/verify_paper_numbers.py re-derives every quantitative claim in the manuscript independently from these artefacts and exits non-zero on any mismatch.
